main_body: A flat dark-green ground patch (4x3 tiles, 64x48 px) with sparse small tufts, red and gold flower dots and darker patches; no standing volume.
top_band: none (terrain tile; the column scan shows one uniform run L~49 over rows 0-47)
evidence: Terrain ground patch, not a standing object. The 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply. The column scan shows one uniform run over all 48 rows, with no object structure to fail. No side face and no elevation drawing. Passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours in total and a median of 12 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and 26 per tile. The paving reference has 7 per tile, but its stones are shaded one by one. The candidate is a near-uniform dark olive base with a repeating pattern of small identical tufts, dark patches and flower dots tiled at 16 px, so it reads as a stamped repeat rather than hand-varied ground. Ground ramps are shallow, with about 3-4 greens, against the grass reference's 5+ with clumps. There is no flat-fill coverage (0%) and the dark edge pixels are tinted, so the outline is not near-black, but the overall density and variety are well below the grass reference. Next to the grass reference it looks thinner and more mechanical, so it fails.
